instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Rinse the rice and cook it according to the package.

Slice the onion thinly. Heat 2 tbsp of the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and 1/4 tsp of the salt and cook for 12 to 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until deep golden. Transfer it to a bowl.
Meanwhile, pat the fish dry and set the fillets in a single layer in a baking dish. Rub them with the remaining tbsp of olive oil, the cumin, 3/4 tsp of the salt and the pepper.
Bake the fish for 12 to 15 minutes, until it flakes when you press it with a fork.
While the fish bakes, toast the pine nuts in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until golden. Transfer them to a small plate right away.

Mince the garlic. Squeeze 3 tbsp of lemon juice into a bowl, add the tahini, garlic and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt, and whisk. It will look thick and pasty at first. Whisk in warm water a splash at a time, about 1/4 cup, until it's thick enough to drizzle. Cut the remaining lemon into wedges and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Transfer the fish to a platter. Spoon the onions over it, drizzle with the tahini sauce and scatter the pine nuts and parsley on top.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of lemon.
Serve with the rice and the lemon wedges.
method_notes: No version cleared 20 ratings, so this leads with The Lemon Bowl's baked fish (4.75 from 4 ratings), which bakes the fillets and drizzles a lemon, garlic and tahini sauce with pine nuts and parsley. Feast in the Middle East and Kavey Eats add caramelized onions and a warm sauce. I kept the lead's sauce and added the caramelized onions and cumin from the others for flavor. The Lemon Bowl card gives two different bake temperatures, so I used 375°F.
